arabic_blocks: [1017] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال: حدثنا غندر قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي إسحاق قال: سمعت الأسود عن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنه قال قرأ النبي ﷺ النجم بمكة فسجد فيها وسجد من معه غير شيخ أخذ كفا من حصى أو تراب فرفعه إلى جبهته، وقال يكفيني هذا فرأيته بعد ذلك قتل كافرا
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Aswad, from ‘Abdullah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited al-Najm in Mecca and prostrated during it. Those with him prostrated, except for an old man who took a handful of pebbles or earth, raised it to his forehead and said, “This is enough for me.” After that, I saw him killed as a disbeliever.

A man among the people took a handful of pebbles or earth, raised it to his face and said, “This is enough for me.” I certainly saw him afterwards, killed as a disbeliever.

arabic_blocks: [1027] حدثنا إبراهيم بن موسى قال: أخبرنا هشام بن يوسف ان ابن جريج أخبرهم قال: أخبرني أبو بكر ابن أبي مليكة عن عثمان بن عبد الرحمن التيمي عن ربيعة بن عبد الله بن الهدير التيمي قال أبو بكر وكان ربيعة من خيار الناس عما حضر ربيعة من عمر بن الخطاب رضى الله تعالى عنه قرأ يوم الجمعة على المنبر بسورة النحل حتى إذا جاء السجدة نزل فسجد وسجد الناس حتى إذا كانت الجمعة القابلة قرأ بها حتى إذا جاء السجدة قال: يا أيها الناس إنا نمر بالسجود فمن سجد فقد أصاب ومن لم يسجد فلا إثم عليه ولم يسجد عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه وزاد نافع عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما إن الله لم يفرض السجود إلا أن نشاء
english_blocks: Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us. He said: Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us that Ibn Jurayj informed them. He said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me, from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Taymi, from Rabi‘ah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn al-Hudayr al-Taymi.
Abu Bakr said: Rabi‘ah was among the best of people.
Concerning what Rabi‘ah witnessed of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

He recited Surat al-Nahl on the pulpit on Friday. When he reached the prostration passage, he came down and prostrated, and the people prostrated. On the following Friday he recited it, and when he reached the prostration passage he said, “O people, we come across passages of prostration. Whoever prostrates has acted rightly, and whoever does not prostrate incurs no sin.” ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, did not prostrate.
Nafi‘ added, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both: “Indeed, Allah has not made prostration obligatory, except if we wish.”

I prayed the late-evening prayer with Abu Hurayrah. He recited “Idha al-sama’u inshaqqat” and prostrated. I said, “What is this?” He said, “I prostrated during it behind Abu al-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, so I will continue to prostrate during it until I meet him.”
